description: Eight tuned bars, each with a rotating tube beneath it: a note blooms as its tube swings through centre, and the eight rotations drift against each other so the pattern never quite repeats

params.text: Sets how fast the tubes turn, 0.02Hz to 2Hz; at the bottom a note blooms about once every twenty-five seconds
Sets how far apart the eight rotation rates are, from all eight together to fully scattered; in Ripple mode it becomes the amount of coupling between neighbours instead
Sets how freely each rate wanders from the rate it was given, rather than holding a fixed period
Sets how the eight rates relate: Ramp raises them smoothly across the row, Stepped gives discrete related values, Random scatters them, Ripple makes a crossing excite its neighbours
Blends the excitation from bowing, where a note is driven continuously, to striking, where it fires at each crossing of centre
Sets how long a note rings and how long a bloom lasts, 0.3 to 8 seconds
Sets the root of the key, twelve semitones
Picks the scale the note degrees are read from
Bends the rotation curve from exponential through linear to logarithmic, which sets how long a tube lingers at the extremes against how quickly it passes centre
Transposes the whole set, -3 to 3 octaves
Sets how wide that note's arc is, 10 to 100 per cent; a narrower arc crosses centre more often, so the note strikes more often

inputs.text: Changes the rotation rate, ±5V added to the rate knob
Changes how far apart the rates are, ±5V added to the spread knob
Changes how far the rates wander, ±5V added to the drift knob
Sets the root, a volt per octave snapped to semitones, added to the root knob
Picks the scale, one volt per scale, added to the scale knob
Locks the rotations to an outside clock; the rate knob then picks how many clock pulses make one rotation, from 32 down to 1
Blends the excitation from bowing to striking, 0-10V, added to the excite knob
Transposes the whole set, one volt per octave, added to the octave knob
Picks how the rates relate, 0-10V across the four modes, added to the relate knob
Bends the rotation curve, ±5V added to the curve knob
Changes the ring and bloom time, one second per volt added to the decay knob

outputs.text: That note's tube rotation itself as a ±5V control voltage, which is the signal blooming the note
That note's sound on its own jack
The left side of the eight notes mixed
The right side of the eight notes mixed
What each of the eight notes is currently tuned to, one polyphonic channel per note
Carries 10V on a channel while that note blooms, one polyphonic channel per note

notes: every rotation crosses centre twice, once going and once coming back, so a struck note fires twice per rotation rather than once
the notes have no envelope of their own: they swell and fade because the tube is moving, so DECAY and the rotation rate together are what shape them
a note takes its pitch as it begins and holds it until it ends, so moving the root, the scale or a degree during a drone is heard on the next bloom rather than as a glide
each note's scale degree and its weight are set on the display, and so is the reseed control; none of them can be reached by clicking for help
menu: Reseed random rates — draws a fresh set of rotation rates, which is what Random mode uses
